chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Ibn Mukan, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Which is the thing in which is the expiation from the oaths?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever you swear upon from what is the righteousness therein, so upon is the expiation when you do not fulfill it; and whatever you swear upon from what is the disobedience therein, so there is not expiation upon you regarding it when you retract from it; and whatever was besides that from what therein is neither a righteousness nor a disobedience, so it is not with anything'.

key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: Expiation or compensation for breaking an oath

ai.seo_question: When is expiation required for an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the obligation of kaffarah depends on the nature of the sworn act: it is due for fulfilling a righteous deed if broken, waived for abstaining from a sin, and irrelevant for neutral matters. This ruling aligns with the Shia juristic principle that oaths regarding obligatory or recommended acts carry weight, while those regarding permissible (mubah) acts do not incur penalty for non-performance. The narration highlights the theological nuance that breaking an oath to commit a sin is rewarded by the act of refraining, thus negating the need for expiation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Ibn Mukan, from Hamza Bin Humran, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘which is the thing in which is the expiation, from the oaths?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whatever you swear upon from what is the righteousness therein, so upon is the expiation when you do not fulfill it; and whatever you swear upon from what is the disobedience therein, so there is not expiation upon you regarding it when you were to retract from it; and whatever was besides that from what therein is neither a righteousness nor a disobedience, so it is not with anything’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from ibn Muskan from Hamzah ibn Humran from Zurarah who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the kind of oath that makes expiation obligatory. He (the Imam) said, ‘If you take an oath for doing something which is a virtuous deed, there is expiation if you do not do it. If you take an oath to do something which is an act of disobedience you do not owe anything if you did not do it; other than these which are not virtuous or of disobedience do not have any valid effect.’”
